CNNs can automatically learn features from raw speech signal and can be used to estimate phoneme class conditional probabilites.

the proposed approach, where the raw speech signal is fed directly to the ANN, can yield better performance when compared to conventional approach, where spectral-based feature MFCCC is extracted and modeled using ANN.

investigating the possibility of using CNNs as a feature extractor and classifier for phoneme classification.
the question of whether the ANN can learn to extract features automatically from raw speech signal and use those features to classify phonemes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed CNN-based approach is a good alternative to conventional approach where, the spectral-based features are extracted from raw speech signal using prior knowledge, and then modeled by ANN.
the proposed approach is a viable alternative to the conventional approach and can be used for ASR system design.

the proposed approach, where the CNN directly learns the phoneme class probability from the raw speech, can be an effective alternative to the conventional approach, which is based on divide and conquer strategy, where feature extraction is performed based on prior knowledge and modeling is performed by ANN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in CNNs, the feature extraction and modeling are done in an integrated manner, and, the feature representation is learned from the raw speech data.
, the proposed CNN architecture can be used as a feature extractor as well as a classifier, and, can be trained end-to-end.
the proposed approach has the potential to replace conventional HMM/ANN ASR systems with HMM/CNN ASR systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of ASR, the divide and conquer strategy of feature extraction and modeling may not be necessary and the raw speech signal itself is sufficient for modeling.
, the divide-and-conquer approach (i.e., feature extraction followed by modeling) in conventional HMM/ANN ASR system may not be necessary.
the proposed CNN approach may provide better feature representation than the conventional approach.
